cpython.source: The base image (python:3.13-slim, pinned by digest in the Dockerfile) builds CPython from source; it is no Debian package.
cpython.reason: What the image of 0.2.0 ships (read 2026-10-26). No advisory against 3.13.16 was known then. When python.org publishes a security release of 3.13, raise this to it and move the Dockerfile's base image to a digest that has it.

ffmpeg.source: PyAV (av 17.1.0) bundles FFmpeg's libraries in its wheel (av.libs).
ffmpeg.reason: What the image of 0.2.0 ships (read 2026-10-26). FFmpeg decodes what devices send: the video worker's H.264 and JPEG decoders are FFmpeg's own, in a process of their own. No advisory against 8.1.1 was known then; an FFmpeg security release means a PyAV that bundles it, and this raised to it.

libvpx.source: PyAV (av 17.1.0) bundles libvpx in its wheel (av.libs).
libvpx.reason: What the image of 0.2.0 ships (read 2026-10-26). aiortc decodes VP8 with it; qKVM asks a JetKVM for H.264 only, so no device's video reaches it today. Gated all the same, so that an older one cannot come back unseen.

libopus.source: PyAV (av 17.1.0) bundles libopus in its wheel (av.libs).
libopus.reason: What the image of 0.2.0 ships (read 2026-10-26). aiortc decodes Opus audio with it; qKVM takes no audio from a device today. Gated all the same, so that an older one cannot come back unseen.

libdav1d.source: PyAV (av 17.1.0) bundles dav1d, FFmpeg's AV1 decoder, in its wheel (av.libs).
libdav1d.reason: What the image of 0.2.0 ships (read 2026-10-26). qKVM decodes no AV1 today. Gated all the same, so that an older one cannot come back unseen.

cryptography-openssl.source: cryptography (50.0.2) links its own OpenSSL into its wheel; it is not Debian's libssl, which the scan sees.
cryptography-openssl.reason: What the image of 0.2.0 ships (read 2026-10-26). It makes the wall's certificates, seals the vault and checks the signatures of updates. No advisory against 4.0.3 was known then.

pylibsrtp-libsrtp.source: pylibsrtp (1.0.0) links libsrtp into its extension.
pylibsrtp-libsrtp.reason: What the image of 0.2.0 ships (read 2026-10-26). It decrypts a JetKVM's media (SRTP). No advisory against 2.7.0 was known then.

pylibsrtp-openssl.source: pylibsrtp (1.0.0) links an OpenSSL of its own into its extension, beside libsrtp; it is neither Debian's libssl nor cryptography's.
pylibsrtp-openssl.reason: What the image of 0.2.0 ships (read 2026-10-26), used for libsrtp's ciphers (AES counter mode and GCM, HMAC-SHA1). OpenSSL releases after 3.5.4 fix advisories in other parts of the library (CMS, PKCS#12, QUIC and TLS among them); none in the ciphers libsrtp calls was known then, and no pylibsrtp with a newer OpenSSL was in the image. When one is, raise this to it.
